transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sasha (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Lena (Head of ML, Hyperion), Arjun (CTO), Priya (Platform Eng)

Summary (auto): POC to demonstrate cost and latency for a routing assistant used in Hyperion's TMS (transport management) workflows. Focus on per-token unit economics, batching and KV/prefix caching, expected QPS, and security/ network constraints for private deployment.

[00:00] Sasha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, super excited. Quick around the room?
[00:10] Lena (Hyperion): Hi, Lena here, head of ML. We're looking to replace a rules+heuristic system with an LLM assistant for routing suggestions and ETA estimates. Main asks are latency and unit cost.
[00:22] Arjun (Hyperion CTO): Arjun, ops/infra owner. We'll need visibility into network patterns and any private deployment implications.
[00:30] Miguel (Redwood SE): Hi all, Miguel from Redwood infra. I'll lead the benchmark and cost modeling side.
[00:40] Sasha: Goal today is to align on success criteria, what sample workload looks like, and what we need to run benchmarks.

[02:05] Lena: Quick background — about 1.2M routing decisions per day right now, peak QPS around 80. Typical prompt sizes are short: 150-600 tokens, but we have occasional long context (up to 2k tokens) for planning. Accuracy threshold is more business KPI oriented — we want suggestion acceptance > 85%.

[04:15] Miguel: Great — for cost modeling we need distribution of token lengths and request rate. If you can provide a histogram (percentiles) that'll let us estimate batching efficiency and KV cache hit rates.
[04:40] Priya: We can pull that from logs. We'll aim to export a week of anonymized request traces. Security's ok with that as long as PII is scrubbed.

[06:12] Sasha: On success criteria quick proposal: latency p95 < 150ms for 512-token paths, cold-start p95 < 500ms, and target marginal cost per 1k tokens served < $0.002 after batching/caching. Thoughts?
[06:40] Arjun: $0.002 per 1k tokens seems aggressive, what's that comparing to?
[06:55] Miguel: It's a proxy; depends on model family, quantization, and effective batching. For hosted inference using a trimmed 7B/13B quantized variant and aggressive batching we can get to low per-token cost. If you need private on-prem with dedicated GPUs the numbers shift up.

[08:30] Lena: We have a budget of roughly $18k/month for inference for this stack initially. How does that map to your per-token estimate?
[08:45] Miguel: Based on rough math: assume 1.2M decisions/day * average 400 tokens/request => 480M tokens/day -> that's enormous, sorry is that right?
[09:05] Lena: Whoops, our decisions are per shipment, but not all decisions call the model. Active calls are closer to 120k/day, not 1.2M.
[09:20] Miguel: OK, 120k/day * 400 tokens = 48M tokens/day ~1.4B tokens/month. At $0.002 per 1k tokens that's about $2.8k/month, which fits budget; but that $0.002 assumes high batching (averaged) and caching. If we run with low batching and no prefix cache it could be 4-8x higher.

[11:00] Sasha: Important to call out batching: if you get sustained QPS we can do continuous batching windows to amortize GPU compute — but for bursty traffic you may need reserved capacity / Dedicated. We should decide whether to run Hosted POC vs Dedicated reserved POC.
[11:28] Arjun: For the POC we'd prefer Hosted to start to avoid infra changes; if it meets SLOs we'll talk Dedicated.

[12:10] Miguel: For the benchmark run I propose: 1) synthetic replay of your anonymized traces w/ true token distribution; 2) run three configs: small model quantized (7B q4), mid (13B q4f), and larger baseline for quality check; 3) metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, effective batching window, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization.

[13:50] Lena: That sounds right. Quality reg is important too — we can provide 200 labeled examples for acceptance testing (we'll call them golden prompts).

[15:00] Miguel: Perfect. A note on KV/prefix caching: for routing state we expect many requests share prefixes (shipment IDs + route context). If you can expose stable prefixes we can measure cache hit rates. With 40-60% prefix hits your effective token generation drops significantly.

[16:30] Priya: Our platform holds route context in Redis — we can surface prefix keys in a sanitized way. Any network constraints for Hosted?
[16:45] Sasha: For Hosted, we need to ensure TLS and provide cert-based mutual auth where needed; we also can do private peering if you want lower network egress. We'll share the security docs.

[18:20] Arjun: What about SLOs and fallbacks? If Redwood service has an outage we need graceful fallback to heuristics.
[18:35] Miguel: Built-in fallback policies are standard — we can set automatic cutoff to heuristics and circuit-breaker. We'll include that in the POC config.

[20:05] Sasha: Back to costs — two knobs matter: batching window (latency vs throughput) and quantization/profile (quality vs compute). For example, increasing batching window from 20ms to 100ms can boost throughput by ~3-4x and reduce per-token cost, but increases tail latency.

[21:30] Lena: Can you give a concrete example number set?
[21:40] Miguel: Sure, approximate: 7B quant q4 on a single GPU: unbatched cost per 1k tokens ~ $0.015; with batching (aggregate 8-12 tokens per CUDA batch effective) ~ $0.003-0.004; with good prefix caching (50% hit) effective ~ $0.0015-0.002. Those are rough but show the levers.

[23:10] Arjun: And for Dedicated?
[23:20] Miguel: Dedicated rented GPUs (reserved) can drop per-token compute cost further but you pay for reserved infra. The break-even depends on sustained QPS; we'll model both hosted billing and dedicated committed cost in the spreadsheet.

[24:50] Priya: Network egress and storage for KV cache — do those add significant cost?
[25:05] Miguel: KV cache is memory/resident on serving nodes — small incremental. Egress only matters if you transfer large context from your VPC; with private peering that's minimized. Storage costs for models are one-time (or image) but negligible vs token compute.

[26:40] Lena: Timeline — we want a POC in about 4 weeks: week 1 data & traces, week 2 benchmark runs, week 3 quality/regression checks, week 4 final cost model & recommendations. Is that realistic?
[27:00] Sasha: Yes that aligns with our typical POC. If we get traces this week we can start bench next Tue/Wed.

[28:30] Miguel: For benchmarks I'll need a commit from you on which endpoints to simulate (sync vs streaming), and whether you require function calls / structured output since that affects tokenization and costs.
[28:55] Lena: We'll start with sync generation and a follow-up for streaming telemetry. Structured output is not required for initial POC.

[30:10] Arjun: For security docs — we need SOC2, KMS options, and audit log retention details.
[30:25] Sasha: We'll share SOC2, and our KMS/HSM integrations doc. Note for Hosted we keep tenant logs for X days by default — we can propose longer retention as an add-on.

[32:00] Miguel: On metrics to capture during bench: tokens generated, prompt tokens vs completion tokens, GPU occupancy, effective batch size, cache hits, p50/p95 latency. We'll output a spreadsheet with line-by-line unit economics and sensitivity analysis across batching/caching scenarios.

[33:20] Lena: Sensitivity analysis is key — show best/median/worst-case depending on cache hit and batch latency.

[34:40] Sasha: Another consideration is model rollouts — for production you may want a canary on a fraction of traffic and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency spikes. We can include rollout config in the final recommendations.

[36:00] Priya: For the Hosted POC do you require any network peering setup?
[36:10] Miguel: Not strictly; we can do it over public endpoints with mTLS. But for lowest egress and security we recommend private peering — that'll be a follow-up depending on infra timelines.

[37:30] Miguel: One more: please confirm the SLA expectations. If p95 is a hard requirement we need to know acceptable failure budget during POC.
[37:45] Arjun: During POC we'll allow 2% errors/failures; for production we'll tighten to 0.5%.

[39:10] Sasha: Recap so far: Hyperion to provide anonymized traces + 200 golden examples + prefix/key patterns; Redwood to run three model configs with and without prefix caching and produce a spreadsheet showing cost per thousand tokens under various batching windows and cache hit rates. POC timeline ~4 weeks.

[40:00] Lena: Sounds good. On the pricing tiers — will you show hosted per-token pricing and an estimate for Dedicated reserved pricing?
[40:12] Miguel: Yes, spreadsheet will have hosted billing lines (per-token/embedding), and a simple TCO model for Dedicated (GPU amortization + infra + support).

[41:30] Arjun: Any concerns about data residency? Our EU clients need data to stay in-region.
[41:42] Sasha: We have region routing and can pin to EU region for the POC. We'll note that in the security doc.

[43:05] Priya: Scheduling — can we do the benchmark window next Wed (2026-06-03)?
[43:15] Sasha: We'll check internal availability but early June looks possible; I'll confirm in the follow-up.

[44:30] Miguel: One small gotcha: tokenization matters. If you intermix languages or domain tokens, your effective token count can vary +/- 15%. We'll account for that in sensitivity analysis.

[45:10] Lena: Ok, thanks. Anything else?
[45:25] Sasha: We'll share the spreadsheet and security deck after this call; Miguel will schedule the bench and we'll reconvene after benchmarks to review.

[46:00] Arjun: Thanks everyone.
[46:05] Lena: Thanks.
[46:10] Miguel: Thanks, bye.

Post-call notes: Redwood to produce a cost model with best/median/worst case based on given traces. Reference artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet (link to be shared by Sasha), security docs (SOC2/KMS).
